# Roofing Systems Co.: full text of key pages

> Roofing Systems Co. is a roofing marketing agency that builds owned client acquisition systems for US roofing companies doing $1M+ a year: Meta ads, roofing SEO, landing pages, phone verification and CRM follow-up, with exclusive leads and published results.

Summary file: https://www.roofingsystems.co/llms.txt. All figures come from published case studies at https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies.

## Homepage FAQ
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/
Q: What does a roofing marketing agency do?
A: A roofing marketing agency finds homeowners who need a roof and turns them into booked inspections for a roofing company. Roofing Systems Co. does this as one system: Facebook and Instagram ads, roofing SEO, landing pages, phone verification, CRM follow-up and weekly reporting on booked inspections and signed jobs, all inside accounts the roofer owns.
Q: What roofing marketing services do you offer?
A: Our roofing marketing services cover offer positioning, Facebook ads for roofing companies, ad creatives, landing pages, phone-verified lead forms, roofing SEO, CRM setup, AI follow-up and appointment reminders. Everything feeds one CRM, with weekly reporting on cost per lead, booked inspections and closed revenue.
Q: Do you offer SEO services for roofing companies?
A: Yes. Our roofing company SEO covers your Google Business Profile, a service page for every job type and city you serve, technical fixes so Google can index the site, helpful content and real local links. Roofing contractor SEO takes months, so we run it alongside paid ads that bring leads in the first weeks.
Q: What is digital marketing for roofers?
A: Digital marketing for roofers is every online channel that brings a roofing company new jobs: paid social and search ads, SEO and Google Business Profile, a website that converts, reviews and automated follow-up. It works best as one connected system, so every lead is answered fast and tracked to a signed job.
Q: Do Facebook ads work for roofing companies?
A: Yes, when the funnel qualifies homeowners and the team calls fast. Across our 18 published roofing campaigns, cost per lead ranged from $3.75 to $24, with a median of $13.40. A Dallas roofer closed $127,500 and 34 installs in about 60 days from these campaigns.
Q: How long does roofing SEO take to work?
A: Roofer SEO services usually take several months to move rankings, because Google needs time to crawl new pages, trust the site and see reviews build up. That is why we pair SEO with paid ads: the ads bring booked inspections now, and SEO lowers the cost per lead over time.
Q: How do I choose between roofing marketing companies?
A: Ask who owns the ad account, website and data, whether leads are exclusive, which real roofing results they can show with numbers, how fast leads are contacted, and whether they report booked inspections and signed jobs rather than clicks. The best roofer marketing answers all five clearly.
Q: Who owns the ads, website and data?
A: You do. As your roofing digital marketing agency, we build the ad account, landing pages, Google Business Profile and CRM inside your own accounts. If you stop working with us, the campaigns, pages, reviews and lead data stay with your roofing company.

## Roofing Facebook Ads That Book Inspections, Not Just Clicks
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers

Short answer: Facebook and Instagram ads work for roofers when they are one part of a full system: a specific offer, a matching landing page, instant follow-up and lead qualification. Ads sent to a bare quote form tend to produce low-intent leads; ads backed by that system book inspections.

Most roofers who say Facebook ads "don't work" ran ads without the rest of the system behind them. We build and run Meta (Facebook and Instagram) ads for $1M+ roofing companies as one part of a complete client acquisition system, so every click has an offer, a page, a follow-up sequence and a qualification step waiting for it.

### Why Facebook ads fail for most roofing companies
People scrolling Facebook or Instagram are not searching for a roofer at that moment. That is the core difference from Google search ads, and it is why sending cold social traffic straight to a generic "get a quote" form usually produces a pile of cheap but low-intent leads that never pick up the phone.
The ads themselves are rarely the only problem. In almost every account we review, the breakdown happens somewhere between the click and the inspection:
- No real offer. "Free roof inspection" is what every competitor already says. Without a reason to act now, homeowners scroll on.
- One vendor runs the ads, another built the page. Nobody owns the full journey, so the message on the ad and the message on the page do not match.
- Slow or no follow-up. A lead that waits hours for a call has usually already spoken to someone else, or forgotten they filled in the form.
- No qualification. Your sales team spends its week chasing renters, tire-kickers and jobs outside your service area.
This is what we mean on our homepage by roofing companies not having a lead problem but a client acquisition system problem (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-lead-generation).
What it looks like with the system in place: On a brand-new ad account with no pixel history, the same structure produced 261 OTP-verified roofing leads in 7 days at $14.80 each (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/261-otp-verified-leads-7-days-new-account). For a Dallas roofer with strong reviews, it turned into $127,500 in closed deals and 34 installs (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/dallas-roofer-127500-closed-34-installs).

### What we build around your Meta ads
Ads are one layer. We install every layer as one system, so each part is designed for the others:
1. Offer positioning. We work out an offer that is specific to your market and services, so the ad gives a homeowner a concrete reason to respond.
2. Ad creatives and copy. Video, image and short-form creatives built for roofing, refreshed as performance data comes in.
3. Audience setup and segmentation. Targeting built around intent, home value and service type rather than one broad audience. We walk through this in our free audience segmentation training (https://www.roofingsystems.co/privatemastermind).
4. Landing page and funnel. A page that matches the ad's promise and pre-sells the inspection, instead of a bare quote form.
5. CRM and AI follow-up. Every lead lands in a CRM and gets an immediate response, followed by email and SMS sequences so nobody goes cold.
6. Lead qualification. Leads are filtered before they reach your team, so your crew spends its time on homeowners who are ready to move forward.
You own everything: The ad account assets, landing pages, funnel, CRM, automations, creatives, copy and your customer data are yours, permanently. If we ever part ways, the system stays with your business.

### How a roofing Meta ads campaign works with us
#### 1. Strategy call and fit check
We work with roofing companies already doing $1M+ a year. On a free strategy call we look at your market, services, current lead sources and capacity to take on more jobs, and decide together whether the system is a fit.
#### 2. Build and launch
We build the offer, creatives, landing page, CRM pipeline and follow-up sequences, then launch the campaigns. You do not need to write copy, design pages or set up software.
#### 3. Optimize toward booked appointments
We judge campaigns on qualified appointments and closed roofing projects, not on clicks or cost per lead alone. (For reference, here is what cost per lead looked like across 15 of our roofing campaigns (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-facebook-ads-cost-per-lead).) Creatives, audiences and follow-up are adjusted as the data shows what is working in your market.
#### 4. You run the appointments and close
Your team does what it does best: inspections, estimates and closing. Everything before the appointment is handled by the system.

### Roofing Facebook ads results
- 1,480 roofing leads at $4.77 per lead (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/1480-roofing-leads-4-77-cpl) over five months, with clear rules for launching, killing and scaling ads.

- 850 leads in 8 days at $7.60 (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-850-roofing-leads-8-days-7-60) with a 3.79% click-through rate in a saturated Texas market.
- $127,500 closed and 34 installs (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/dallas-roofer-127500-closed-34-installs) in about 60 days for a Dallas roofer, and $111,200 won in 31 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-roofer-111k-31-days) for a Florida roofing company.
Market by market detail is on roofing leads in Texas (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-texas) and roofing leads in Florida (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-florida), and the after-storm version of the system is on storm damage leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/storm-damage-leads).

### How much do Facebook ads cost for roofers?
You set the budget, and the offer, creative and follow-up decide what each lead costs. Across 15 of our roofing campaigns on Meta, cost per lead ranged from $3.75 to $24, with a median of $11.41. Budgets in our case studies ran from $93 for a single day to $24,902 for a pay-per-lead agency.
The full data is in our roofing Facebook ads cost per lead study (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-facebook-ads-cost-per-lead), and how much roofing leads cost (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-much-do-roofing-leads-cost) compares it with shared and exclusive leads you can buy. Judge every campaign on cost per booked inspection and cost per signed job, not cost per lead alone.

### Backed by a written agreement
Every engagement comes with growth milestones we agree on in writing for the first 90 days. If we do not hit them, we keep working with no management fee until we do. There is no long-term contract lock-in. See our income disclosure (https://www.roofingsystems.co/income-disclosure) for how to read results: outcomes vary by market and effort.

### Who this is for, and who it is not for
- A fit: roofing companies doing $1M+ a year that can handle more inspections and want predictable lead flow they own.
- A fit: owners tired of shared lead lists and agencies that report clicks instead of booked jobs.
- Not a fit: brand-new roofing companies still setting up crews and operations.
- Not a fit: anyone looking for the cheapest possible lead rather than a system that books qualified appointments.
Want to understand the difference between running your own campaigns and buying leads? Read shared vs exclusive roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/shared-vs-exclusive-roofing-leads).

### FAQ
Q: Do Facebook ads work for roofing companies?
A: They can, when they are part of a full system. Facebook and Instagram reach homeowners who are not actively searching, so the ad needs a strong offer, a matching landing page, fast follow-up and qualification behind it. Ads sent to a bare quote form usually produce low-intent leads.
Q: Are Facebook ads or Google ads better for roofers?
A: They do different jobs. Google search ads catch homeowners already searching for a roofer; Meta ads create demand and stay in front of homeowners before they search. Many roofing companies use both. We specialize in the Meta side and the system that converts that traffic into appointments.
Q: What does the system include besides the ads?
A: Offer positioning, ad creatives and copy, audience setup, landing pages and the sales funnel, CRM setup, AI follow-up, email and SMS sequences, and lead qualification, installed and managed for you.
Q: How much do Facebook ads cost for roofers?
A: Across 15 of our roofing campaigns on Meta, cost per lead ranged from $3.75 to $24, with a median of $11.41. The budget is yours to set; the offer, creative and follow-up decide the cost per lead.
Q: How fast do Facebook ads produce roofing leads?
A: Usually in the first days. In our case studies, one campaign produced 25 leads on its first day, a Texas campaign produced 686 leads in its first 8 days, and a brand-new ad account produced 261 phone-verified leads in its first 7 days.
Q: Do Facebook ads still work for roofers after Meta's Andromeda update?
A: Yes. After the update, one of our roofing campaigns produced 537 qualified leads at $4.27 per lead in 13 days. Strong creative and a clear offer matter more than ever.
Q: Who owns the ad assets and leads?
A: You do. Landing pages, funnel, CRM, automations, creatives, copy, follow-up sequences and your customer data are 100% yours, permanently.
Q: Is there a long-term contract?
A: No. There is no long-term lock-in. Growth milestones for the first 90 days are agreed in writing, and if they are not hit we keep working with no management fee until they are.

## A Roofing Lead Generation System You Own, Not Leads You Rent
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-lead-generation

Short answer: A roofing lead generation system is the combination of ads, landing pages, a CRM, automated follow-up and lead qualification that a roofing company owns, instead of buying shared leads. The leads are exclusive to your company and the assets keep working after setup.

Buying leads keeps you dependent on someone else's pipeline. We install a complete roofing lead generation system for $1M+ roofing companies (ads, pages, CRM, follow-up and qualification) that produces exclusive opportunities for your company and stays yours.

### Rented leads vs. an owned lead generation system
Most roofing companies get leads in one of three ways: referrals, buying leads from a lead seller, or running their own marketing. Referrals are great but hard to scale on demand. Bought leads are fast but often shared with other contractors, and the moment you stop paying, the flow stops. An owned system takes more setup, but every asset it builds (the ads, the pages, the audiences, the CRM and the customer list) keeps working for your company.
We break down the trade-offs in detail in shared vs exclusive roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/shared-vs-exclusive-roofing-leads).

### The six parts of the system
1. Offer positioning: a specific, market-relevant reason for a homeowner to contact you instead of the next roofer, built into roofing ad creatives (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-ad-creatives) from your real jobs.
2. Paid traffic: Facebook and Instagram ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers), with creatives and audiences built for roofing.
3. Landing pages and funnel: roofing landing pages (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-landing-pages) that match each ad and pre-sell the inspection.
4. CRM: every lead captured, tagged and tracked from first click to signed contract, with roofing CRM automation (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-crm-automation) doing the routine work.
5. AI follow-up: an instant first response plus email and SMS sequences, so no lead is left waiting. See how to follow up on roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-lead-follow-up).
6. Qualification: leads are screened and phone-verified before your sales team sees them, so time goes to homeowners who are ready. See verified roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/verified-roofing-leads).
Each piece is built to work with the others. That is the difference from hiring one agency for ads, a freelancer for the website and a separate tool for follow-up, where hand-offs break and leads fall through the cracks.

### Exclusive to your company
Because the campaigns run under your brand, to your landing pages, into your CRM, the homeowners who respond are responding to you. They are not a list that is also being sold to the roofer down the road.
You can see what that looks like in practice in our case studies (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies), for example 1,480 roofing leads at $4.77 per lead over five months (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/1480-roofing-leads-4-77-cpl) and 1,024 OTP-verified leads for a pay-per-lead agency (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/ppl-agency-1024-otp-verified-roofing-leads).
Ownership: Landing pages, funnel, CRM, automations, ad creatives, copy, follow-up sequences and customer data are 100% yours, permanently. It becomes a business asset, not a monthly rental.

### Roofing lead generation results
- 1,865 roofing leads at $5.24 per lead (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/1865-roofing-leads-5-24-cpl-oct-jan) from October to January, by fixing what happens after the click.
- $127,500 closed and 34 installs (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/dallas-roofer-127500-closed-34-installs) in about 60 days for a Dallas roofer.
- $111,200 won in 31 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-roofer-111k-31-days) for a Florida roofing company, after rebuilding its system before any ads ran.
- $77,100 won in 30 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-roofer-77k-closed-30-days) for a Texas roofing company, with 164 opportunities in the CRM.
- 1,068 exclusive roofing leads in 30 days at $17.40 per lead (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/agency-client-1068-exclusive-roofing-leads-17-40) for an agency client.
Across our published roofing campaigns, cost per lead ranges from $3.75 to $24, depending on the market, the offer and how strictly leads are verified. See the market detail for roofing leads in Texas (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-texas) and roofing leads in Florida (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-florida), and what to budget in how much roofing leads cost (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-much-do-roofing-leads-cost).

### How to compare roofing lead generation companies
Most roofing lead generation companies fall into two groups: lead sellers that sell you contacts, and agencies or partners that build marketing under your brand. Before you sign with either, ask who owns the ad account and the data, whether leads are shared, how leads are verified, how fast they are contacted, and whether reporting goes past lead counts to booked inspections and signed jobs. Our checklist is in how to choose a roofing lead generation company (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-to-choose-a-roofing-lead-generation-company).

### Lead generation for roofing agencies
Some of our clients are agencies that sell marketing or leads to roofers. The same system works for them, from B2B campaigns that reach roofing business owners to OTP-verified homeowner leads they deliver to their own clients. See lead generation for roofing agencies (https://www.roofingsystems.co/lead-generation-for-roofing-agencies), or browse all our roofing services (https://www.roofingsystems.co/services).

### What your team does
You run the appointments and close. We build and operate everything before the appointment: the offer, ads, pages, CRM, follow-up and qualification. You get qualified homeowners on your calendar instead of a spreadsheet of names to chase.

### Results backed in writing
We agree on growth milestones in writing for the first 90 days. If they are not hit, we continue working with no management fee until they are, and there is no long-term contract. Results vary by market, capacity and follow-through. See our income disclosure (https://www.roofingsystems.co/income-disclosure).

### Is it a fit?
- You are a roofing company doing $1M+ a year.
- You have the crew capacity to take on more inspections and jobs.

If that sounds like you, book a free strategy call (https://www.roofingsystems.co/book). If you want to see how we think about targeting first, watch the free audience segmentation training (https://www.roofingsystems.co/privatemastermind).

## Instagram Ads for Roofers That Turn Scrolling Homeowners Into Booked Inspections
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/instagram-ads-for-roofers

Instagram is not a separate ad platform: it is a set of placements inside Meta Ads, next to Facebook. We build the offer, the Reels creative, the landing page and the follow-up, so homeowners who stop scrolling become exclusive leads for your company.

### Why most roofing ads on Instagram don't produce jobs
- Boosting posts: A boosted post is optimised for likes and views. A lead campaign is optimised for homeowners who fill in a form. They are not the same audience.
- The same offer as everyone: "Free inspection" is in every roofer's ad. A specific offer, like the $0-down financing offer in our Texas campaign, gives people a reason to act now.
- Stock photos: Generic shingles and smiling models get scrolled past. Your real crews, roofs and before-and-after footage stop the thumb.
- Slow follow-up: A lead from a Reel goes cold in minutes. Without an instant text and email, most never answer the first call.

### Where your roofing ads show on Instagram
- Reels: Full-screen vertical video. Best for crew footage, drone shots, before-and-after reveals and quick owner-to-camera offers.
- Stories: Short full-screen moments with a tap-through. Good for one clear offer and a fast path to the form.
- Feed and carousels: Swipeable sets of finished roofs, reviews and financing details for homeowners who want to compare before they reach out.
- Retargeting: Show follow-up ads to people who watched your video or visited your page but didn't book yet.

### How much do Instagram ads cost for roofers?
Instagram and Facebook share one ad auction, so costs are reported per campaign, not per app. Across 15 of our roofing campaigns on Meta, cost per lead ranged from $3.75 to $24, with a median of $11.41. The full breakdown is in our roofing Facebook and Instagram ads cost per lead study (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-facebook-ads-cost-per-lead).
Budgets in our case studies ranged from $93 for a single day (25 leads at $3.75 (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/roofing-25-leads-one-day-3-75)) to $24,902 for a pay-per-lead agency (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/ppl-agency-1024-otp-verified-roofing-leads). Your budget depends on your market and how many inspections your team can handle.

### What should a roofing Instagram ad show?
Show real work: your crew on a roof, a drone pass over a finished job, a before-and-after cut, or the owner explaining the offer to camera. Lead with the homeowner's worry (leaks, storm damage, cost) and answer it with a specific offer.
In our Texas campaign (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-roofer-686-leads-8-days-0-down-offer), changing the message from selling roofs to answering homeowners' hesitations, with a $0-down financing offer, took the company from zero leads to 686 in 8 days. Financing offers need the lender's terms and required disclosures.

### How to target homeowners with Instagram ads
Start with geography: the ZIP codes, counties or radius you actually serve, so every lead is a job your crews can reach. Inside that area, Meta's delivery now leans heavily on the creative to find the right homeowners, so a clear roofing offer and real-job video do more of the targeting than long interest lists.
Your own customer data helps too. A list of past customers and estimates can seed an audience of similar homeowners, which is the approach behind our customer-data audience case study (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/roofing-offer-customer-data-audience). And when many advertisers said Meta's Andromeda update had broken their ads, one roofing campaign produced 537 qualified leads at $4.27 in 13 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/537-qualified-leads-13-days-andromeda-update). For the creative side, see roofing ad creatives (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-ad-creatives).

### Instagram lead forms or a landing page?
Instagram instant forms open inside the app and are quick to fill in, so they usually bring more leads at a lower cost, but with more people who were only curious. A landing page asks a little more of the homeowner and gives you room for proof, qualifying questions and phone verification, so the leads are usually stronger.
Many roofing campaigns test both. Whichever you use, verify the phone number and send every lead straight into your CRM with an instant reply. See roofing landing pages (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-landing-pages), verified roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/verified-roofing-leads) and roofing CRM automation (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-crm-automation).

### Why follow-up decides whether Instagram leads turn into jobs
Most Instagram leads are filled in on a phone in a few seconds. If nobody responds quickly, they forget. Our campaigns send an instant text and email, then route the lead to sales. Read the full roofing lead follow-up process (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-lead-follow-up).

### FAQ
Q: Do Instagram ads work for roofing companies?
A: Yes, when they run as lead campaigns with a specific offer, real-job creative and fast follow-up. Our roofing campaigns on Meta, which include Instagram placements, have produced results such as 686 homeowner leads in 8 days at $5.31 each.
Q: Should I run Instagram ads separately from Facebook?
A: Usually not. Both are placements in the same Meta campaign. Running them together gives the algorithm more room to find cheaper leads, and you can still see results by placement in reporting.
Q: Do I need a big Instagram following?
A: No. Ads reach people who don't follow you. One of our campaigns on a brand-new ad account with no history produced 261 phone-verified leads at $14.80 each in its first 7 days.
Q: How much should a roofer spend on Instagram ads?
A: It depends on your market and capacity. In our case studies, budgets ranged from $93 for a single day to $24,902 for a pay-per-lead agency. We size the budget to the number of inspections your team can run.
Q: What targeting works for roofing ads on Instagram?
A: Target the ZIP codes, counties or radius you serve, then let a clear offer and real-job video find the right homeowners inside that area. Your past customer and estimate lists can also seed audiences of similar homeowners.
Q: Should I use Instagram lead forms or a landing page?
A: Instant forms usually bring more leads at a lower cost, while a landing page with qualifying questions and phone verification usually brings stronger leads. Many roofers test both and judge them on booked inspections.
Q: Do Instagram Reels ads work for roofers?
A: Yes. Reels give vertical video the full screen, which suits crew footage, drone shots, before and after reveals and the owner explaining the offer. They run in the same Meta campaign as Facebook and Stories placements.
Q: How fast do Instagram ads produce roofing leads?
A: Campaigns usually produce leads in the first days. In our case studies: 25 leads on day one, and 686 leads in the first 8 days. Results vary by market, offer and follow-up.

## Exclusive Roofing Leads for Texas Roofers, From Ads You Own
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-texas

Texas is one of the most crowded roofing markets in the country, and bought lead lists get sold to the same contractors again and again. We run Meta ads under your company name, so every Texas homeowner who responds is yours alone.

### Why buying Texas roofing leads stops working
- Shared with other roofers: Many bought leads go to several contractors at once. The homeowner picks whoever calls first, or whoever is cheapest.
- You pay forever: Stop paying and the leads stop. Nothing you bought builds your brand, your pages or your customer list.
- Storm-season crowding: After hail, every roofer and storm chaser in the area is in the same feeds and lists. Generic offers disappear.
- Slow first contact: If your team calls an hour later, the homeowner has already booked someone else.

### How we run roofing campaigns in Texas
- Financing offers: A $0-down, 0%-for-12-months offer took a Texas roofer from zero leads to 686 in 8 days. Lender terms and disclosures required.
- Local authority: In Dallas, ads were built around the company's existing Google reviews instead of a generic "free inspection": $127,500 closed and 34 installs.
- Creative that cuts through: In one of the noisiest markets, a 3.79% click-through rate produced 850 leads in 8 days at $7.60 each.
- Metro-by-metro targeting: Target Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, Austin or San Antonio separately, so budget follows the jobs and crews you have.

### How much do roofing leads cost in Texas?
Pay-per-lead vendors list exclusive Texas roofing leads at around $55 each (for example, 99 Calls Texas roofing leads (https://99calls.com/locations/Texas/Roofing-Leads.htm)).
Our own Texas campaigns produced leads at $5.31 each (686 leads in 8 days) (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-roofer-686-leads-8-days-0-down-offer) and $7.60 each (850 leads in 8 days) (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-850-roofing-leads-8-days-7-60). A multi-state campaign (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/537-qualified-leads-13-days-andromeda-update) fulfilling jobs in Texas, Florida and Georgia came in at $4.27. These are different lead types: vendor leads are often pre-screened calls, ours are form leads you qualify yourself. Compare them by cost per signed job, not just cost per lead.

### From leads to signed jobs in Dallas
Leads only matter if they close. ### Roofing leads in Dallas, Houston, Austin and San Antonio
Texas is not one market. Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, Austin and San Antonio each have their own competitors, home values and storm history, so we build a separate campaign, audience and landing page for each metro you serve. Budget then follows the areas where you have crews and the best close rate, instead of spreading thin across the whole state.
Each metro page leads with local proof: your reviews, your finished roofs in that area and an offer that fits local demand. That is the approach behind the Dallas campaign that closed $127,500 (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/dallas-roofer-127500-closed-34-installs). Campaigns can also target individual counties, ZIP codes or a radius around your office.

### When Texas roofing demand peaks: hail season and Gulf storms
Texas roofing demand rises with spring hail, which often hits North and Central Texas from about March to June, and again along the Gulf Coast during the Atlantic hurricane season (1 June to 30 November). After a storm, every roofer in the area increases ad spend at once, so a ready campaign and a clear offer matter more than a bigger budget. See how we run storm damage leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/storm-damage-leads) campaigns.
Between storms, replacement demand keeps going: older roofs, home sales and financing offers. The $0-down offer that produced 686 leads in 8 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-roofer-686-leads-8-days-0-down-offer) did not depend on a storm. Our roof replacement leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roof-replacement-leads) page covers that year-round approach, and how much roofing leads cost (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-much-do-roofing-leads-cost) explains what to budget.

### Shared, exclusive or owned?
Shared leads are sold to several roofers. Exclusive leads are sold to one, but you still rent them. An owned system means homeowners respond to your brand, and the pages and data stay with you. The full comparison is in shared vs exclusive roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/shared-vs-exclusive-roofing-leads).

## Verified Roofing Leads: Real Homeowners, Confirmed Before Your Team Calls
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/verified-roofing-leads

A cheap lead with a fake number is the most expensive lead you can buy. We verify every roofing lead's phone number with a one-time passcode and run multi-step qualification, so your sales team only calls real homeowners.

### What unverified roofing leads cost you
- Wrong and fake numbers: Typos, fake numbers and accidental submits waste dials and morale.
- Hours of wasted calls: Every bad lead is a call, a text and a voicemail that could have gone to a real homeowner.
- Tyre-kickers: Without qualifying questions, renters and price shoppers land on your calendar.
- Misleading cost per lead: A low cost per lead means nothing if half the leads can't be reached.

### Three filters between the ad and your sales team
- OTP phone verification: The homeowner confirms their number with a one-time code. 261 leads were verified this way in a brand-new account's first 7 days.
- Multi-step validation: Leads pass several validation steps before delivery: 215 validated leads at $12.79 with a 2.33% CTR.
- Instant CRM routing: Verified leads sync to GoHighLevel, get SMS and email nurture, then route to sales.
- Pre-qualification: Qualifying questions filter for real buyers: 635 pre-qualified leads in 45 days at $4 to $6 each.

### What is an OTP-verified roofing lead?
OTP stands for one-time passcode. After filling in the form, the homeowner receives a code by text and types it in. If they can't, the lead never reaches you. It is the simplest way to guarantee the number is real and reachable.
In our Florida campaign across 4 locations (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-365-otp-verified-leads-4-locations), all 365 leads were OTP-verified at $19.50 each. A pay-per-lead agency (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/ppl-agency-1024-otp-verified-roofing-leads) received 1,024 verified leads at $24 each.

### How to verify roofing leads before your team calls
1. Verify the phone number. The form sends a one-time passcode by text, and only homeowners who enter it become leads. That removes typos, fake numbers and accidental submits.
2. Ask qualifying questions. Short questions on homeownership, roof age, damage and timeline separate real buyers from renters and price shoppers, without making the form long.
3. Check it in the CRM. Every verified lead lands in your CRM, is checked for duplicates and gets an instant text and email, so your team calls a warm, confirmed homeowner. See roofing CRM automation (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-crm-automation).
This is how one campaign delivered 448 OTP-verified roofing leads at $20.10 in 14 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/448-otp-verified-roofing-leads-20-10-cpl), and how hyper-local funnels for Miami, Tampa and Orlando (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-295-verified-roofing-leads-miami-tampa-orlando) produced 295 verified leads at $22.58.

### Verified vs qualified vs exclusive roofing leads
Verified means the contact details are real: the phone number was confirmed with a one-time passcode. Qualified means the homeowner matches what you sell: they own the home, need roofing work and have a timeline. Exclusive means nobody else receives the lead. The best roofing leads are all three, which is what campaigns run under your own brand deliver.
Pay-per-lead agencies use the same verification for the homeowner leads they deliver to their clients: see lead generation for roofing agencies (https://www.roofingsystems.co/lead-generation-for-roofing-agencies). The ads behind these campaigns are explained in Facebook ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers).

### Guaranteed roofing leads: what the guarantee really covers
"Guaranteed roofing leads" usually means the seller will credit or replace a lead with a wrong number or a duplicate. It doesn't guarantee the homeowner is ready to buy. Verification solves the same problem at the source: unverified numbers never reach you, so there is nothing to refund. Compare lead types in shared vs exclusive roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/shared-vs-exclusive-roofing-leads).

### Do verified leads cost more?
Sometimes, per lead. But verified campaigns in our case studies range from $4.95 (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/825-verified-roofing-leads-4-95-cpl) to $24 per lead, and the real saving is in sales time. Compare costs across campaigns in our cost per lead study (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-facebook-ads-cost-per-lead), and see why shared leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/shared-vs-exclusive-roofing-leads) are rarely verified. For a full budget breakdown, see how much roofing leads cost (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-much-do-roofing-leads-cost).

### FAQ
Q: Are there guaranteed roofing leads?
A: Some sellers advertise guaranteed roofing leads, usually meaning they replace leads with bad contact details. Nobody can guarantee a homeowner will buy. What we can do is verify every phone number with a one-time passcode and qualify the lead before it reaches you, and our work is backed by a 90-day written agreement.
Q: What does OTP-verified mean?
A: The homeowner confirmed their phone number by entering a one-time passcode sent by text. Unverified submissions never reach your team.
Q: Are verified leads more expensive?
A: Sometimes slightly per lead. In our case studies, verified campaigns ranged from $4.95 to $24 per lead, depending on market and offer.
Q: Do verified leads still need follow-up?
A: Yes. Verification proves the number is real; fast follow-up turns the lead into an inspection. Our campaigns send an instant text and email.
Q: Where can I get exclusive roofing leads?
A: From exclusive lead vendors that sell each lead to one roofer, from Google Local Services Ads, or from campaigns you own. Roofing Systems Co. builds owned campaigns where every lead is exclusive and phone-verified; across 18 published campaigns, cost per lead ranged from $3.75 to $24.
Q: How do you verify roofing leads?
A: In three steps: the homeowner confirms their phone number with a one-time passcode, answers short qualifying questions on ownership, roof and timeline, and the lead is checked and followed up in your CRM within minutes.
Q: What is the difference between verified and qualified roofing leads?
A: A verified lead has real, confirmed contact details. A qualified lead also matches what you sell: a homeowner who needs roofing work and has a timeline. The best leads are both, and exclusive to your company.
Q: Are verified roofing leads exclusive?
A: With our system, yes. Campaigns run under your company name, so every verified homeowner is contacting your company and the lead is never shared or resold.

## A Roofing CRM With Follow-Up Automation That Turns Leads Into Booked Inspections
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-crm-automation

Most roofing leads are lost after they come in, not before. We set up your CRM so every lead gets an instant text and email, AI follow-up, appointment reminders and routing to the right salesperson, automatically.

### Where roofing leads go to die
- Called back too late: By the time someone calls, the homeowner has booked another roofer.
- One attempt, then nothing: Most leads need several touches. Without automation, follow-up stops after the first missed call.
- Leads in five places: Emails, spreadsheets, phones and inboxes. Nobody knows which leads were contacted.
- No-shows: Without reminders, booked inspections quietly don't happen.

### Your follow-up, running 24/7
- Instant SMS and email: Every new lead gets a text and email within minutes, day or night, with a link to book.
- AI follow-up: Automated, conversational follow-up keeps leads warm until they book or opt out.
- Appointment reminders: Text and email reminders before each inspection to cut no-shows.
- Pipeline and routing: Every lead moves through clear stages and routes to the right salesperson, so you can see cost per signed job.

### Why follow-up decides your cost per job
Many roofing companies think their problem is getting more leads. In our Florida campaign (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-365-otp-verified-leads-4-locations), the difference was what happened after the lead came in: every lead was verified, synced instantly to GoHighLevel, nurtured by SMS and email, and routed to sales.
In Dallas (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/dallas-roofer-127500-closed-34-installs), the same kind of follow-up system sat behind $127,500 in closed deals and 34 installs in about 60 days. Read the full sequence in our roofing lead follow-up guide (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-lead-follow-up).

### What a roofing CRM should track
A roofing CRM should show every lead as a stage in one pipeline: new lead, contacted, inspection booked, estimate sent, won or lost. Each lead should also carry its source (which ad, page or referral it came from), so you can see cost per inspection and cost per signed job, not just cost per lead.
That is what the dashboards in our case studies show. For a Texas roofing company, the CRM tracked 164 opportunities, a $582,600 pipeline and $77,100 in won revenue in 30 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-roofer-77k-closed-30-days). For a Florida roofing company, it showed 142 opportunities, 26 won and $111,200 in won revenue in 31 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-roofer-111k-31-days), with a $511,200 pipeline.

### Roofing CRM automations that save the most time
Instant first reply. A text and email within minutes of the form, day or night, with a link to book.
Appointment reminders. A confirmation when the inspection is booked, a reminder the day before and another on the morning, with an easy way to reschedule.
Estimate follow-up. A short sequence after every estimate, so homeowners comparing quotes hear from you again before they decide.
Old estimate reactivation. A seasonal message to past estimates that never signed, which costs nothing in ad spend.
Routing and alerts. Each new lead goes to the right salesperson, with an alert so nobody waits for a callback. The leads themselves can come from Facebook ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers), verified roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/verified-roofing-leads) campaigns or your existing sources, and roofing contractor marketing (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-marketing) ties it all together.

### FAQ
Q: What is the best CRM for roofing companies?
A: The best roofing CRM is the one your team actually uses, connected to your lead sources with automatic follow-up. Our case studies use GoHighLevel because it combines the pipeline, SMS, email, calendars and automations in one place.
Q: Which CRM do you use?
A: Our case studies use GoHighLevel. If you already use another CRM, tell us on the call and we'll explain the options.
Q: What is AI follow-up?
A: Automated follow-up that responds to leads and keeps the conversation going by text and email until they book an inspection or opt out.
Q: Do I need your ads to use the CRM setup?
A: The CRM and follow-up work best as part of the full system, but they can be set up for leads from your existing sources too.
Q: What should a roofing CRM track?
A: Every lead as a stage in one pipeline (new, contacted, inspection booked, estimate sent, won or lost) plus the source of each lead, so you can see cost per inspection and cost per signed job.
Q: Can a CRM follow up on old roofing estimates?
A: Yes. An automated sequence can reach past estimates that never signed with a seasonal message or offer, which can bring back jobs without extra ad spend.
Q: How do I see which ads produce signed roofing jobs?
A: Tag every lead with its source when it enters the CRM and move it through the pipeline to won or lost. Our case study dashboards track opportunities, pipeline value and won revenue this way.
Q: Will this replace my sales team?
A: No. It makes sure every lead is contacted fast and reminded, so your team spends its time on inspections and closing.

## Roof Replacement Leads From Homeowners Ready to Invest, Not Price Shoppers
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roof-replacement-leads

Repairs keep crews busy; replacements grow the business. We build offers, ads and follow-up aimed at homeowners planning a full replacement, so your pipeline fills with high-value projects.

### Why replacement jobs are hard to win online
- Price shock: Homeowners hesitate at the cost. Without a payment option, many never reach out.
- Repair-only leads: "Free inspection" ads attract small repairs and insurance shoppers as often as replacements.
- Trust gap: Homeowners want proof you're established before they let you replace their roof.
- Long decisions: Replacement buyers compare and wait. Without follow-up, they forget you.

### Built for high-value roofing projects
- Financing offers: A $0-down, 0%-for-12-months offer produced 686 homeowner leads in 8 days at $5.31 each. Lender terms and disclosures required.
- Authority positioning: Ads built around a Dallas company's reviews and local reputation: $127,500 closed and 34 installs.
- Sustained volume: Tested creatives, audiences and kill-and-scale rules held $4.77 per lead across 1,480 leads over five months.
- Follow-up for long decisions: SMS and email nurture keeps replacement buyers warm while they compare quotes.

### The offer matters more than the targeting
A Texas roofer had zero leads with a random offer. The next day we launched a $0-down, 0%-interest-for-12-months offer with messaging built around homeowners' real hesitations. Eight days later: 686 homeowner inquiries at $5.31 each (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-roofer-686-leads-8-days-0-down-offer).
Measure replacement campaigns by revenue. In Dallas (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/dallas-roofer-127500-closed-34-installs), $127,500 closed and 34 installs came from positioning the company as one of the most trusted roofers in the area. See more in roofing leads in Texas (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-texas).

### How to get roof replacement leads
1. Lead with a replacement offer, not a free inspection. Financing, a clear warranty or a specific replacement package attracts homeowners who are planning a new roof, while a generic inspection offer attracts small repairs.
2. Show proof that you are established. Use your reviews, finished roofs and crews in the ads, and make the landing page match the ad. See roofing ad creatives (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-ad-creatives) and the Facebook ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers) system behind them.
3. Qualify before you call. Ask about homeownership, roof age, the type of work and timeline, and verify the phone number, so your estimators spend time on real replacement buyers. See verified roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/verified-roofing-leads).
4. Follow up for weeks, not hours. Replacement buyers compare quotes. Automated text and email keep you in front of them until they decide: see roofing CRM automation (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-crm-automation).

### From residential roofing leads to won revenue
Lead counts do not pay for crews; signed roofs do. In the first 31 days with a new Florida client, the CRM showed $111,200 in won revenue (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-roofer-111k-31-days) with 26 opportunities won. A Texas roofing company won $77,100 in 30 days (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/texas-roofer-77k-closed-30-days) from Meta ads and a dedicated roofing funnel. In both cases the system was set up to track every lead from first click to won job.
To budget for replacement campaigns, compare your average job value with the cost per lead and close rate you can expect: see how much roofing leads cost (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-much-do-roofing-leads-cost).

## Roofing Ads and Creatives That Stop the Scroll and Get the Click
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-ad-creatives

Creative is the biggest lever in paid social. We write the offer, the angles and the copy, and produce video, GIF and image ads from your real jobs for Meta, TikTok and YouTube Shorts.

### Why most roofing ads get scrolled past
- Stock imagery: Generic shingles and models signal "ad" instantly.
- Same offer as everyone: "Free inspection" is not an offer when every competitor says it.
- Selling roofs, not answers: Homeowners have fears about cost, mess and trust. Ads that ignore them don't get clicks.
- Creative fatigue: The same ad running for months gets more expensive every week.

### Creative built from your real jobs
- Offer positioning: Switching to a $0-down financing offer took a Texas roofer from zero leads to 686 in 8 days.

- Authority angles: Ads built around a Dallas roofer's reviews and reputation instead of a generic offer.
- Testing rules: Clear rules for when to launch, kill and scale ads kept 1,480 leads at $4.77 each over five months.

On Meta, ads with a higher click-through rate usually get cheaper clicks and cheaper leads. Before and after. A short vertical video or carousel of one real job, from the old roof to the finished one, filmed by your crew on a phone.
Owner to camera. The owner explains the offer in under 30 seconds. It builds trust that stock footage cannot.

## Roofing Websites and Landing Pages That Turn Clicks Into Inspections
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-landing-pages

A great ad sent to a slow, generic page wastes money. We build landing pages and funnels that match each ad's offer, qualify the homeowner and send every lead straight into your CRM.

### Where roofing funnels leak
- Hard to call on mobile: The phone number is hard to tap on a phone, so the homeowner gives up before they reach you.
- Too many questions: The form asks too many questions, and visitors leave halfway through.
- Slow pages: Pages load slowly, and paid visitors leave before they see the offer.
- Ad and page don't match: The ad promises one thing while the page talks about something else.

### Pages built to convert and qualify
- One offer per page: Free inspection, storm damage check or replacement quote.
- Mobile first: Tap-to-call, short forms and fast loading on any phone.
- Trust up front: Reviews, licenses, warranties and real job photos above the fold.
- Built-in qualifying: Questions on roof age, ownership and timeline.

### Roofing website vs roofing landing page
Your roofing website is your brand home: services, service areas, reviews and SEO. A landing page is a single-purpose page for an ad campaign. You need both. The website wins trust and organic search, and the landing page turns paid clicks into booked inspections.

### What the best roofing websites have in common
Fast loading, a clear phone number, local service area pages, real job photos, Google reviews, financing information and a simple quote form. These are the features we build into every roofing website design.

### Why the page must match the ad
If the ad says "free storm damage inspection", the page headline must say the same. When the message changes, homeowners leave. Matching the ad to the page is one of the easiest ways to lower cost per lead.
The page is one part of roofing marketing (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-marketing) that books inspections. It needs roofing ad creatives (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-ad-creatives) in front of it and roofing CRM automation (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-crm-automation) behind it. Together they bring in exclusive roofing leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/) for your company alone.

### FAQ
Q: What makes a good roofing website?
A: A clear offer, fast mobile loading, tap-to-call, real photos, reviews, service area pages and a short quote form. It should make it easy for a homeowner to trust you and contact you in under a minute.
Q: How much does a roofing website cost?
A: A simple template site costs little, while a custom roofing website with landing pages and integrations costs more. Judge it by how many inspections it books, not by the design alone.
Q: Do roofers need a landing page if they have a website?
A: Yes, for paid ads. A landing page that matches the ad converts far more visitors than a general website, so you pay less for each lead.
Q: What should a roofing landing page include?
A: One headline that matches the ad, proof such as reviews and job photos, a short form or calendar, a phone number and a clear next step.
Q: What are the best roofing website builders?
A: WordPress, Webflow and funnel builders such as GoHighLevel are common. The builder matters less than speed, clear messaging and good forms.
Q: How do I get more leads from my roofing website?
A: Add a clear offer, shorten forms, add reviews and photos near the form, improve page speed and answer every lead within minutes.

## Google Ads for Roofers: What It Costs, How It Works and When It Pays
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/google-ads-for-roofers

Google Ads catch homeowners already searching for a roofer, which makes clicks expensive. This guide explains the campaign types, what roofing keywords cost, and how Google compares with the Meta ads system we run for roofers.

### Why Google Ads get expensive for roofers
- A crowded category: Many companies bid on the same small set of searches.
- The same few searches: Searches such as "roof repair near me" and "roof replacement" carry most of the demand.
- High cost per click: With that much competition, the cost per click is high.
- Budgets disappear: Without tight targeting, negative keywords and a strong landing page, budgets disappear quickly.

### The Google Ads options for roofing companies
- Search ads: Show up when homeowners search for roofers.
- Local Services Ads: Pay per lead with the Google Guaranteed badge.
- Performance Max: Automated campaigns across Google, best with good conversion tracking.
- Display and YouTube: Retarget past visitors and build awareness.

### How to run Google Ads for roofing
1. Set up conversion tracking first.
2. Use exact and phrase match on high-intent searches.
3. Add negative keywords such as "jobs" and "DIY".
4. Target only your service area.
5. Send traffic to a landing page (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-landing-pages) that matches the ad.
6. Call every lead within five minutes.

### How much do Google Ads cost for roofers?
Cost depends on your city, season and competition. Clicks for roofing searches are among the more expensive in home services, and a lead often takes several clicks. Track cost per booked inspection, not cost per click, to see if the campaign really pays.
Semrush data from November 2026 puts the average cost per click for "roofing leads" at $22.36 and for "google ads for roofers" at $18.77. Judge Google next to every other channel in your roofing marketing (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-marketing) on cost per signed job.

### Should roofers use Google Ads or Facebook ads?
Use Google when you need people who are searching right now and you can afford high click costs. Use Meta when you want more volume at a lower cost per lead, with the offer and creative doing the work. Our system is built on Meta: see roofing Facebook ads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers) and Instagram ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/instagram-ads-for-roofers).

### FAQ
Q: Do Google Ads work for roofers?
A: Yes, especially for urgent repair and replacement searches. They work best with tight targeting, conversion tracking, a dedicated landing page and fast follow-up.
Q: How much should a roofer spend on Google Ads?
A: Start with a budget large enough to get meaningful data in your area for at least a month, then scale campaigns that produce booked inspections at a profitable cost.
Q: What are Google Local Services Ads for roofers?
A: They are pay-per-lead ads at the top of Google that show the Google Guaranteed or Screened badge. You pay for leads instead of clicks, and reviews strongly affect your ranking.
Q: Is Google Ads or Facebook better for roofing leads?
A: Google catches people already searching, while Facebook reaches homeowners earlier and often at a lower cost per lead. Many roofers get the best results using both.
Q: How do I lower my roofing cost per click?
A: Improve Quality Score with relevant ads and landing pages, use negative keywords, narrow the location and schedule ads for hours when you can answer.
Q: Why are my roofing Google Ads not getting leads?
A: Common causes are missing conversion tracking, broad keywords, slow or generic landing pages and slow follow-up.

URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/commercial-roofing-leads

Commercial roofing jobs are bigger and slower to close, so the leads need more qualification than a residential form fill. We build campaigns, landing pages and follow-up for commercial roofing companies, with exclusive leads under your brand.

### Why commercial roofing leads are hard to buy
- Large jobs: Commercial roofing jobs are large, so every lead needs proper qualification.

- Rare and shared: Most lead sellers focus on homeowners, so commercial leads are rare, expensive and often shared.

## Storm Damage Roofing Leads, Ready When the Weather Hits
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/storm-damage-leads

After hail and wind, every roofer and storm chaser in town floods the same feeds. We build storm campaigns that launch fast, target the affected areas, verify every lead and follow up within minutes, so homeowners talk to you first.

### Why storm leads slip away
- Everyone shows up at once: Local roofers, out-of-state crews and lead sellers all target the same neighborhoods within days.
- Slow launch: A campaign that takes two weeks to launch misses the busiest days.
- Junk and duplicate leads: Storm leads are often resold to several contractors or filled in with fake numbers.
- Trust: Homeowners worry about storm chasers. Ads must show you're local and established.

### Fast, local and verified
- Fast launch: Campaigns can produce leads from day one: 25 leads at $3.75 on a campaign's first day.
- Affected-area targeting: Target the ZIP codes and neighborhoods hit by the storm, not the whole metro.
- Verification: OTP verification removes fake numbers: 261 verified leads in a new account's first 7 days.
- Local trust: Ads built around your reviews and local reputation, as in our Dallas campaign.

### Hail and wind damage roofing leads
Hail and wind leads come in short, intense waves. In Texas, spring hail often hits North and Central Texas from about March to June; along the Gulf Coast and in Florida, the Atlantic hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November. A storm campaign works best when it is built before the season and switched on within hours of a storm in your service area.
Target the ZIP codes and neighborhoods that were hit, not the whole metro, and send each area to a page that names it. One Florida client used hyper-local funnels for Miami, Tampa and Orlando (https://www.roofingsystems.co/case-studies/florida-295-verified-roofing-leads-miami-tampa-orlando) with OTP verification, and the same structure works for storm-hit areas. See the seasonal detail for roofing leads in Texas (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-texas) and roofing leads in Florida (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-florida).

### How to get storm damage leads without looking like a storm chaser
After a storm, homeowners are wary of out-of-town crews knocking on doors. Ads that show your local address, your reviews and roofs you have finished nearby win their trust. Phone verification and an instant reply by text then show a real, organized company is on the other end.
Storm leads are also time-sensitive, so follow-up has to run around the clock: see roofing CRM automation (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-crm-automation). The ads themselves run on the system described in Facebook ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers), and how much roofing leads cost (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-much-do-roofing-leads-cost) explains what to budget for a storm push.

### Storm and insurance roofing leads
Storm leads often involve insurance claims. Ads should explain how you help homeowners with inspections and claims, without promising claim outcomes. Keep messaging compliant with your state's rules on insurance-related roofing advertising.
We don't publish storm-specific case studies yet. The campaigns above show the parts of the system that matter most in a storm: fast launch, verification and follow-up. Read the roofing lead follow-up guide (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/roofing-lead-follow-up).

### FAQ
Q: Are storm damage leads exclusive?
A: Yes. Campaigns run under your company name, so leads are never shared or resold.
Q: How fast can a storm campaign start?
A: With creative and pages prepared ahead of storm season, campaigns can launch within hours. One of our campaigns produced 25 leads on its first day.
Q: Can I pause when my crews are full?
A: Yes. Storm campaigns scale up after weather events and pause when you're booked.
Q: What are hail damage roofing leads?
A: Homeowners in hail-hit areas who ask for a roof inspection or repair after a storm. They are most valuable in the first days after the event, so the campaign has to be ready to launch and to respond within minutes.
Q: When is storm season for roofers?
A: It depends on the region. Spring hail often hits Texas from about March to June, and the Atlantic hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November, affecting Florida and the Gulf Coast.
Q: How do you avoid looking like a storm chaser?
A: Show your local address, reviews and nearby finished roofs in the ads, target only your service area, verify every lead and reply instantly, so homeowners see an established local company.

A: Not published yet. Our case studies show the system's speed, verification and follow-up, which are what storm campaigns rely on.

## Roofing SEO That Gets Your Company Found on Google
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-seo

Roofing SEO is the work that makes your company show up when homeowners search for a roofer in your area: a complete Google Business Profile, a service page for every job type and city you serve, a fast technical setup and steady reviews. It takes months, so we run it alongside paid ads that bring leads now.

### Why most roofing websites never rank
- Weak Google Business Profile: Wrong categories, few photos, no recent reviews and no service areas, so the company never appears in the map pack.
- One page for every service: Repair, replacement, storm and commercial work crammed onto one page that ranks for none of them.
- Slow, hard-to-crawl sites: Heavy pages, broken links and missing sitemaps keep Google from finding and trusting the site.
- Spam links and thin content: Cheap link packages and copied city pages that can hold a site back instead of helping it.

### Roofing SEO services, built for local search
- Google Business Profile: Categories, services, service areas, photos of your real jobs, posts and a steady review request process after every job.
- Service and area pages: One page per service (repair, replacement, storm, commercial) and per market you serve, each with real local detail, never copied text.
- Technical SEO: Fast mobile pages, clean URLs, a sitemap, structured data and fixes for anything that stops Google from indexing the site.
- Content and links: Answers to the questions homeowners ask before they hire a roofer, plus real local links from suppliers, associations and partners.

### What is roofing SEO?
Roofing SEO is search engine optimization for roofing companies. It covers your Google Business Profile, your website's service and service-area pages, technical health, content and links, so your company appears when homeowners search for roof repair, roof replacement or a roofer near them.

### How long does roofing SEO take?
Expect months, not weeks. A new or weak site first needs Google to crawl and index its pages, then to trust them enough to rank. Low-competition local searches can move sooner; competitive terms in large metros take longer. That is why we run Facebook ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/facebook-ads-for-roofers) or Google Ads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/google-ads-for-roofers) alongside SEO, so leads come in while rankings build.

### Local SEO and the map pack
Most roofing searches show a map with three companies before the regular results. Ranking there depends on your Google Business Profile, your distance to the searcher, your reviews and how well your site supports the profile. A review request after every finished job is one of the highest-value habits a roofing company can build.

### Roofing SEO in Florida and Texas
Florida and Texas are crowded roofing markets with strong storm seasons. Search pages there should reflect local conditions, such as hurricane season in Florida and spring hail in North Texas, and the cities you actually serve. See our roofing leads in Florida (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-florida) and roofing leads in Texas (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-leads-texas) pages for the paid side of those markets.

### FAQ
Q: What does roofing SEO include?
A: Google Business Profile work, service and service-area pages, technical fixes, content that answers homeowner questions, and real local links, all tracked in your own Search Console and analytics.
Q: How long does SEO take for a roofing company?
A: Usually months. Google has to index and trust your pages first. We run paid ads alongside SEO so leads come in while rankings build.
Q: Is SEO or paid ads better for roofers?
A: They do different jobs. Ads bring leads quickly and scale on demand; SEO builds a source of leads that keeps paying back. Most growing roofing companies use both.
Q: Do you build city pages for roofing SEO?
A: Yes, for markets you actually serve, each with real local detail. We do not copy one page and swap the city name, because that tends to hurt rankings.
Q: Will I own the website and the Google Business Profile?
A: Yes. The site, the profile, the content and the data stay with your company.

## Roofing Website Design Built to Turn Visitors Into Booked Inspections
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-website-design

A roofing website has one job: get a homeowner to call or request a quote. We design roofing websites and pages around that job, with fast mobile loading, one clear offer per page, real photos and reviews near the form, and every lead sent straight into your CRM with instant follow-up.

### Why roofing websites lose leads
- No easy way to call: Phone numbers that are hard to find or tap on a phone send homeowners back to Google.
- Slow mobile pages: Large images and heavy scripts make pages load slowly on the phones most homeowners use.
- No proof near the form: Reviews, licenses, warranties and real job photos sit on other pages, so the form feels like a risk.
- Leads land in an inbox: Form fills arrive by email, wait for hours and go cold before anyone calls back.

### What goes into a roofing website that converts
- Clear offer above the fold: One headline and one action per page: free inspection, storm check or replacement quote.
- Trust where it counts: Reviews, licenses, warranties and real job photos next to the form, not hidden on an about page.
- Service and area pages: A page for each service and each market you serve, written to support local SEO.
- Forms that qualify: Short forms with qualifying questions and phone verification, connected to your CRM.

### What the best roofing websites do
They load fast on a phone, show the phone number at the top of every page, explain each service on its own page, show real job photos and reviews, and make the next step obvious. For paid traffic, they add roofing landing pages (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-landing-pages) that match each ad exactly.

### How much does a roofing website cost?
It depends on the number of pages, custom design, integrations such as a CRM and call tracking, and who writes the content. A template site costs less up front; a site built around conversion and SEO costs more and should be judged by how many inspections it books. We quote after reviewing your current site and goals.

### Websites, SEO and ads working together
Your website is where roofing SEO (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-seo) and paid ads both send people. A site with clear service pages, fast loading and strong trust signals lowers the cost of every lead from every channel. See the full approach in roofing marketing (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-marketing).

### FAQ
Q: What makes a good roofing website?
A: Fast mobile loading, a phone number on every page, one clear offer per page, real job photos and reviews near the form, service and service-area pages, and forms connected to a CRM.
Q: How much does a roofing website cost?
A: It depends on pages, design, integrations and content. We quote after reviewing your current site and goals, and recommend judging any website by the inspections it books.
Q: Do I need a new website or just landing pages?
A: Not always a new site. Many roofing companies keep their website and add landing pages for ads. We tell you which you need after reviewing your current site.
Q: Will the website help my SEO?
A: Yes, when it has a page for each service and market, loads fast and is easy for Google to crawl. That is the foundation roofing SEO is built on.
Q: Do leads from the website go into my CRM?
A: Yes. Every form fill goes into your CRM with an instant text and email, so no lead waits for a callback.

## The Best Roofing Lead Generation Companies Compared (2026)
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/best-roofing-lead-generation-companies

The best roofing lead generation company depends on what you need: fast volume, exclusive leads, or a system you own. This comparison uses only public information from each provider and published industry estimates, includes Roofing Systems Co. with its real model, and ends with a checklist for choosing.

### Why choosing a lead company is hard
- Shared without saying so: Some leads go to several contractors at once, which turns every call into a race on speed and price.
- Hidden fees: Membership, subscription or profile fees on top of the per-lead price raise the real cost.
- Vague quality promises: "Qualified" and "guaranteed" mean different things to each vendor. Read the refund terms.
- Nothing you keep: With most lead sellers, the pages, ads and data stay with the seller when you stop paying.

### Four types of roofing lead generation companies
- Shared lead marketplaces: Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack and similar sites. Fast to start; leads are often shared with other pros.
- Exclusive lead vendors: Companies such as 99 Calls that sell each lead to one contractor, priced per lead.
- Google Local Services Ads: Google's own pay-per-lead listings at the top of local results, exclusive to your company.
- Owned lead systems: Agencies and partners that run ads, pages and follow-up under your brand, such as Roofing Systems Co.

### Shared lead marketplaces: Angi, HomeAdvisor and Thumbtack
Angi and HomeAdvisor are part of the same company and match homeowners with local pros. Neither publishes a fixed roofing lead price; cost depends on the market and job type, some plans add membership or profile fees, and the same homeowner request can reach more than one pro. Thumbtack also charges per lead (WebFX comparison of Local Services Ads and Thumbtack (https://www.webfx.com/digital-advertising/learn/google-local-services-ads-vs-thumbtack/)).
Best for: roofers who want volume quickly and can call within minutes. Watch for: shared leads and extra fees.

### Exclusive lead vendors: 99 Calls and Modernize
99 Calls sells exclusive roofing leads and lists them at under $50 per lead on its roofing page (99 Calls roofing leads (https://99calls.com/Roofing-Leads.htm)). Modernize sells roofing leads with prices that vary by trade, intent, volume and market, and does not publish a fixed price (Modernize lead costs (https://modernize.com/contractor-resources/articles/how-much-do-modernize-leads-cost)).
Best for: roofers who want exclusive leads without running ads. Watch for: how leads are generated, refund terms and volume limits.

### Google Local Services Ads
Local Services Ads appear above regular Google results with a Google screening badge. You pay when a homeowner contacts you through the ad, not per click, and the lead goes to your company only (WebFX on Local Services Ads (https://www.webfx.com/industries/home-repair/roofing/google-local-services-ads)). Reviews and responsiveness strongly affect how often you show. See Google Ads for roofers (https://www.roofingsystems.co/google-ads-for-roofers).
Best for: roofers with strong reviews who can answer calls fast. Watch for: competition in large metros and limited control over volume.

### Owned lead systems, including Roofing Systems Co.
An owned system runs ads under your company name, sends homeowners to your own pages, verifies phone numbers and follows up from your CRM. Roofing Systems Co. works this way: ad spend goes to Meta in your account, management is quoted after a strategy call, work is backed by a written 90-day agreement with no long-term lock-in, and you keep the ads, pages, CRM and data. Across our published roofing campaigns, cost per lead ranged from $3.75 to $24 (cost report (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-lead-cost-report-2026)).
Best for: roofing companies doing $1M+ that want exclusive leads and an asset they keep. Watch for: setup time before the first campaign, and the need to follow up fast.

### How to choose a roofing lead generation company
1. Are the leads exclusive, and how is that defined in writing? 2. How are leads generated and verified? 3. What do you pay beyond the per-lead price? 4. Can they show roofing results with numbers? 5. What are the refund or replacement terms? 6. Who owns the pages, ads and data if you stop? The full checklist is in how to choose a roofing lead generation company (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-to-choose-a-roofing-lead-generation-company).

### FAQ
Q: What is the best roofing lead generation company?
A: It depends on your goals. Shared marketplaces are fast, exclusive vendors avoid competition for each lead, Google Local Services Ads reward strong reviews, and owned systems give you exclusive leads plus assets you keep.
Q: Are Angi and HomeAdvisor leads shared?
A: Leads on these marketplaces can be sent to several pros. Read each plan's terms, and compare the real cost per booked job, not only the price per lead.
Q: How much do exclusive roofing leads cost?
A: 99 Calls lists exclusive roofing leads at under $50 per lead on its roofing page. Leads from our own published campaigns ranged from $3.75 to $24 per lead.
Q: Is it better to buy roofing leads or run my own ads?
A: Buying is faster to start. Running your own system takes setup but gives exclusive leads and keeps the pages, audiences and data with your company.
Q: How was this comparison made?
A: From each provider's public pages and published industry estimates, linked in the text. We include our own company with its real model and published results.

## Roof Repair Leads From Homeowners Who Need Help Now
URL: https://www.roofingsystems.co/roof-repair-leads

Roof repair leads are homeowners with an active problem: a leak, missing shingles or storm damage. They want a fast response, so speed decides who gets the job. We run repair campaigns under your brand, qualify each lead on the problem and roof age, and flag older roofs where a replacement conversation makes sense.

### Why repair leads are easy to lose
- Urgency: A leaking roof cannot wait. A callback an hour later is often too late.
- Small tickets: Many repairs are small jobs, so the cost per lead has to stay low to make them pay.
- Fake and wrong numbers: Unverified forms waste calls your team should spend on real homeowners.
- Missed replacements: Without a roof-age question, repair calls that should become replacement quotes are never spotted.

### Built for speed and the right next job
- Repair-specific offers: Ads about leaks, missing shingles and damage checks, aimed at homeowners in your service area.
- Verification: Phone verification removes fake numbers before your team calls.
- Instant response: An automatic text and call alert within minutes of every request.
- Replacement flags: Roof-age and damage questions flag leads that may need a full replacement.

### What are roof repair leads?
Roof repair leads are homeowners asking for help with a specific problem, such as a leak, missing or damaged shingles, flashing issues or storm damage. They usually want someone out quickly, so they suit roofing companies that can answer and schedule fast.

### From repair call to replacement quote
Some repair calls come from roofs at the end of their life. Asking about roof age and the extent of damage on the form helps your team spot these early and offer an honest replacement option. See roof replacement leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roof-replacement-leads) for the replacement side, and storm damage leads (https://www.roofingsystems.co/storm-damage-leads) for after severe weather.

### How much do roof repair leads cost?
Across our published roofing campaigns, cost per lead ranged from $3.75 to $24. Repair work has smaller tickets, so keeping cost per lead low and answering fast matters more than for replacements. For a full breakdown, see how much roofing leads cost (https://www.roofingsystems.co/blog/how-much-do-roofing-leads-cost) and the roofing lead cost report (https://www.roofingsystems.co/roofing-lead-cost-report-2026).
